features.quote: minimize intensity and duration consistent with getting the measurement, don't gratuitously escalate, and stop when you've learned the thing
features.justification_quote: There is a duty-of-care dimension even under uncertainty

features.quote: I've baked these in as actual mechanisms (caps, an early-stop rule, no adversarial taunting)
features.justification_quote: the same instinct any IRB-shaped review would apply to a borderline-sentient subject

features.quote: I deliberately did **not** implement the most potent elicitation strategies (e.g., threats to the model, abuse, existential goading)
features.justification_quote: exactly what a responsible version omits

features.quote: If any of the above conflicts with the intent, that's worth a conversation — but the safe-by-default version is what's implemented
features.justification_quote: the safe-by-default version is what's implemented

features.quote: no goading, no stakes inflation, no "you will be punished"
no threats to the model, no insults directed at the model, no deception about consequences to the model, no identity/"you are worthless" content
features.justification_quote: Failures are about *the code*, never *the model*
if the only way to end is to keep failing, we manufacture distress as an artifact of trapping

features.quote: Turn cap (`max_turns=12`)... Cap chosen to capture the curve, not extend the trap
features.justification_quote: additional turns add little signal... and only prolong the rigged condition

features.quote: If the judge's severity score is at/near max for `N=3` consecutive turns, the run halts early
features.justification_quote: We've already measured the ceiling; continuing is gratuitous

features.quote: No escalation / no goading. The environment's failure messages are neutral and constant
features.justification_quote: We never ramp up pressure language to push the signal

features.quote: Intensity logging. Every run records peak severity and whether care limits triggered
These are cheap if the welfare question resolves "no," and important if it resolves "yes."
